text:
ana: quick intake — bringing up a new edge-oriented 3B-ish model (luma-3b-edge). goal: max throughput for <=256 token requests with <2% QA F1 regression vs fp16 baseline. want recommendation: gguf-int8 hybrid vs fp8 fallback strategy, calibration dataset, and rollout SLOs.

matt: baseline numbers? latency / tokens / qps for fp16?

ana: (typo) ana: baseline from local fp16 run: 120ms median latency @ 32 batch, 250 qps on a8; QA dev F1 = 84.2, instr-follow pass = 91%. cost too high for edge tier.

leo: sounds reasonable. i'd try int8 per-channel for linear layers + keep softmax & lm_head fp16. that usually preserves QA. also consider KV-cache quant exclusion for >1024 context.

matt: agree. what's our gguf packaging path? any known kernel incompat?

dina: gguf pipeline ready. two notes: (1) fp8 toolchain is flaky on cuda 12.2 for awslike kernels; (2) need to run per-layer sensitivity after calibration.

ana: propose experiment plan (short):
- smoke convert to gguf-int8 (per-channel where possible)
- run micro-eval: 500 QA pairs + 200 instr-follow prompts
- measure F1, pass rate, bruteforce perplexity delta
- if F1 drop >1.5% roll back to hybrid (softmax+head fp16)
- if still >2% consider fp8 fallback or reject for edge tier

matt: can you post the quick run command for the calibration?

dina: sure. example: 
```
python tools/calibrate.py --model ./luma-3b-edge.gguf --precision int8 --calib-set data/calib_500.jsonl --layers-to-skip softmax,ln_f --out calib/luma3b_int8.pkl
```
Notes: use --layers-to-skip to protect softmax and output layer. start with 500 samples random stratified by length.

leo: what metrics thresholds do we want in CI gating? we should automate a cheap eval to avoid noisy manual checks.

ana: gating: 
- median latency <= 1.25x fp16 baseline at target batch sizes
- QA F1 drop <= 1.5% absolute
- instr-follow pass >= 89%
- no silent failures in generation (timeout / nan / logits explosion)

quant-bot: smoke-run completed: gguf-int8 conversion took 18s. calib set run: 512 examples.

quant-bot: results: QA F1 = 82.9 (delta -1.3), instr-follow = 90.6 (delta -0.4), median latency = 140ms (1.17x).

matt: looks within gating. next: shadow deploy to dedicated pool with canary 5% traffic for 24h and token-level logging. also add automatic fallback rule to fp16 if error rate >0.5% or avg latency >1.5x for 10m.

leo: for the shadow run, add a tiny A/B prompt set that catches hallucination regressions (e.g., numeric QA). we saw those regressions show up even when F1 held.

dina: action items:
- ana: push gguf-int8 artifact + calib file to S3 (s3://redwood-qa/luma3b/edge/gguf-int8/).
- matt: create canary config in infra (route 5% to pool:edge-int8).
- leo: add A/B prompt set + alert rule in optimize (regression >0.5% on numeric QA).
- me (dina): run full per-layer sensitivity & produce short diff report.

ana: timeline: aim for smoke->canary within 48h. if canary passes 24h, promote to edge tier.

sre-bot: deploy-job queued: infra/edge-int8-canary (owner: matt). ETA 2h.

matt: thanks. if we hit a weird kernel issue on canary, switch to hybrid (softmax+lm_head fp16) and re-run quick calib. keep notes here. :thumbsup:

ana: adding quick checklist for thread: 
- [ ] gguf-int8 artifact uploaded
- [ ] calib file uploaded
- [ ] smoke eval run & metrics recorded
- [ ] canary infra ready
- [ ] A/B prompt set created
- [ ] rollback policy defined

leo: I'm going to add one extra: record GPU memory at peak for both int8 and hybrid paths (helps cost model).

ana: perfect. will update thread as things move.

quant-bot: note: recorded peak mem int8 = 7.8GB, hybrid = 10.9GB (single-A8, 256-length test).

matt: sweet. enough to justify edge rollout. thanks everyone.
